description: Full implementation TODO covering Supabase backend, all interactive features, real-time subscriptions, and two new pages that need to be built from scratch.

todos.title: Initialize Supabase project and install SDK
todos.description: Create a new Supabase project at supabase.com. Install @supabase/supabase-js in the React project. Create /src/lib/supabase.js that exports a single client initialized with VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY from .env. This client is the single import used everywhere in the app.

todos.title: Run full database schema migration
todos.description: In Supabase SQL Editor run the complete schema that creates all tables: profiles, courses, schedule_slots, tasks, study_logs, streaks, burnout_snapshots, calendar_events, friendships, messages, study_sessions, study_session_participants, notes, note_sections, note_collaborators, notifications, user_presence. Include uuid primary keys (gen_random_uuid()), all foreign keys with ON DELETE CASCADE where appropriate, NOT NULL constraints, and default timestamps.

todos.title: Enable Row Level Security on all tables
todos.description: Enable RLS via ALTER TABLE x ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on every table. Policies: (1) profiles — users can SELECT/UPDATE only their own row (id = auth.uid()). (2) tasks, courses, notes, study_logs, burnout_snapshots, calendar_events, streaks, schedule_slots — SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE only where user_id = auth.uid(). (3) friendships — SELECT/UPDATE where requester_id = auth.uid() OR addressee_id = auth.uid(). (4) messages — SELECT where sender_id OR receiver_id = auth.uid(); INSERT where sender_id = auth.uid(). (5) notifications — SELECT/UPDATE only user_id = auth.uid(). (6) note_collaborators — SELECT if user_id = auth.uid() OR note is owned by auth.uid(). (7) study_session_participants — SELECT if user_id = auth.uid() OR session host_id = auth.uid().

todos.title: Create updated_at auto-trigger
todos.description: Create a reusable PostgreSQL trigger function handle_updated_at() that sets NEW.updated_at = now(). Attach it as a BEFORE UPDATE trigger on: profiles, tasks, courses, friendships, notes, streaks, user_presence. This prevents needing to manually pass updated_at in every UPDATE call from the frontend.

todos.title: Create React Router v6 routes with protected route wrapper
todos.description: Set up React Router v6 with routes: / (Landing), /login, /dashboard (protected), /friends (protected), /friends/add (protected — new page), /friends/:friendId/profile (protected — new page), /tasks (protected), /notes (protected), /notes/:folder/:slug (protected), /settings/profile (protected). Create a ProtectedRoute component that calls supabase.auth.getSession(). If no session redirect to /login. If session and user is on /login redirect to /dashboard.

todos.title: Create global AuthContext with session listener
todos.description: Create /src/context/AuthContext.jsx. On mount: call supabase.auth.getSession() to restore existing session and supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange() to listen for SIGNED_IN/SIGNED_OUT. When SIGNED_IN fires, fetch the user's profile row from public.profiles and store in context. Expose { session, user, profile, loading, signOut }. The signOut function calls supabase.auth.signOut() then navigates to /. All pages use useAuth() hook.

todos.title: Build /login page with Magic Link and Google OAuth
todos.description: Create /src/pages/Login.jsx. Show two sign-in options: (1) Magic Link: email input + 'Send Magic Link' button calls supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email, options: { emailRedirectTo: window.location.origin + '/dashboard' } }). On success show 'Check your email for the magic link.' (2) Google OAuth: 'Continue with Google' button calls supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({ provider: 'google', options: { redirectTo: window.location.origin + '/dashboard' } }). Handle loading and error states. Style consistently with GRIT's neo-brutalist design (black borders, yellow accents).

todos.title: Auto-create profile, streak, and presence rows on new sign-up
todos.description: Create a PostgreSQL function handle_new_user() and trigger on_auth_user_created (AFTER INSERT on auth.users). The function inserts: (1) profiles row: id=NEW.id, email=NEW.email, full_name from NEW.raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name' (populated by Google OAuth), avatar_url from raw_user_meta_data->>'avatar_url'. (2) streaks row: user_id=NEW.id, current_streak=0, longest_streak=0. (3) user_presence row: user_id=NEW.id, status='offline'. This ensures all required rows exist the moment a user signs up.

todos.title: Enable Google OAuth provider in Supabase dashboard
todos.description: In Supabase Dashboard → Authentication → Providers → Google: enable it and enter Client ID + Client Secret from a Google Cloud Console OAuth app. In Google Console, add the Supabase callback URL (https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback) to Authorized Redirect URIs. Add http://localhost:5173 to Authorized JavaScript Origins for local dev. Also enable Email provider for magic links.

todos.title: Sign out from sidebar and topbar profile dropdown
todos.description: The sidebar bottom area shows the user's avatar + name from AuthContext.profile. Clicking it (or the gear icon next to it) opens a small menu with 'Profile Settings' (navigates to /settings/profile) and 'Sign Out'. The topbar 'ALFIAN' button at top-right also opens a dropdown with the same options. Sign Out calls authContext.signOut() which runs supabase.auth.signOut() and redirects to /.

todos.title: Load and prefill user profile on /settings/profile
todos.description: On /settings/profile mount, fetch: supabase.from('profiles').select('*').eq('id', user.id).single(). Prefill all form inputs: full_name, bio, university, major, daily_study_goal_hours (slider), preferred_study_time (pill buttons — active state). Show the user's avatar_url as the profile image, or a colored letter box using the first letter of full_name if no avatar. Show skeleton loaders while fetching.

todos.title: Save profile changes on SAVE button
todos.description: On SAVE click, call supabase.from('profiles').update({ full_name, bio, university, major, daily_study_goal_hours, preferred_study_time }).eq('id', user.id). Show loading spinner on the SAVE button during the request. On success: show a toast notification 'Profile saved!', and refresh the profile in AuthContext (so sidebar name updates instantly). On error, show the error message inline.

todos.title: Upload avatar photo via camera icon
todos.description: Clicking the camera icon overlay on the profile avatar in /settings/profile triggers a hidden file input (accept='image/*'). On file select: (1) Upload to Supabase Storage bucket 'avatars' with path `${user.id}/avatar.${fileExtension}` using supabase.storage.from('avatars').upload(path, file, { upsert: true }). (2) Get the public URL. (3) Update profiles.avatar_url. (4) Update local display immediately. Create 'avatars' bucket in Supabase Storage with public read policy.

todos.title: Load dashboard stat cards (tasks done, study hours, streak, GPA)
todos.description: On /dashboard mount run 4 parallel queries: (1) Tasks done this week: supabase.from('tasks').select('id', { count: 'exact' }).eq('user_id', uid).eq('status', 'done').gte('updated_at', startOfWeek). (2) Study hours: supabase.from('study_logs').select('duration_minutes').eq('user_id', uid).gte('logged_date', startOfWeek), then sum and divide by 60. (3) Streak: supabase.from('streaks').select('current_streak').eq('user_id', uid).single(). (4) GPA: from AuthContext profile.current_gpa. Display in the 4 stat cards. Show numeric skeleton during load.

todos.title: Load upcoming deadlines card on dashboard
todos.description: Query: supabase.from('tasks').select('id, title, priority, due_date').eq('user_id', uid).neq('status', 'done').gte('due_date', today).order('due_date', { ascending: true }).limit(3). Format due_date as 'Tomorrow' if it is today+1, otherwise 'Mar 12' format. Priority badge: HIGH=red, MEDIUM=orange, LOW=green. 'View all tasks →' navigates to /tasks. Empty state: 'No upcoming deadlines!'

todos.title: Load course overview card on dashboard
todos.description: Query: supabase.from('courses').select('id, name, credits, grade, color').eq('user_id', uid).order('created_at').limit(3). Show each course with its credits and grade badge. Count total active courses from the full courses count query (not limited). 'View all courses →' navigates to /tasks with the Academic Load tab pre-selected (pass ?tab=academic-load in the URL). Empty state: 'Add your first course in Tasks → Academic Load'.

todos.title: Dynamic dashboard calendar with events
todos.description: The calendar shows the current month. Fetch: (1) supabase.from('calendar_events').select('*').eq('user_id', uid).gte('event_date', firstDayOfMonth).lte('event_date', lastDayOfMonth). (2) supabase.from('tasks').select('id, title, due_date').eq('user_id', uid).gte('due_date', firstDayOfMonth).lte('due_date', lastDayOfMonth). Render event label chips inside the matching date cells. Prev/next arrows change displayed month and re-fetch. Today's date has a highlighted black cell.

todos.title: Dynamic welcome card — greeting, streak, due-this-week count
todos.description: Welcome card shows: (1) Time-based greeting: 'Good Morning' (6–12), 'Good Afternoon' (12–17), 'Good Evening' (17–24). (2) User's full_name from AuthContext.profile. (3) Streak from streaks table. (4) Tasks due this week count: supabase.from('tasks').select('id', { count: 'exact' }).eq('user_id', uid).neq('status', 'done').gte('due_date', today).lte('due_date', today+7). Display 'You have X tasks due this week. Keep up the momentum!'

todos.title: Daily motivation quote
todos.description: Create a motivations table (id, quote, author) and seed it with 20+ classic quotes via a SQL INSERT in the migration. On dashboard load, fetch one random quote: supabase.rpc('get_random_motivation') — create a simple SQL function that does SELECT * FROM motivations ORDER BY random() LIMIT 1. Display in the gradient motivation card. Alternatively call a free public quotes API like quotable.io with no backend needed.

todos.title: Load all tasks in My Tasks tab with real-time updates
todos.description: Query: supabase.from('tasks').select('*').eq('user_id', uid).order('due_date', { ascending: true, nullsFirst: false }). Display in the table with columns: Name, Priority badge, Status badge, Due Date, Delete icon. Show '7 tasks total · X active' in header (active = status != 'done'). Subscribe to real-time changes: supabase.channel('tasks').on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'tasks', filter: `user_id=eq.${uid}` }, handler). On change refetch or apply delta to local state.

todos.title: Add new task inline with '+ New Task' button
todos.description: Clicking '+ New Task' appends an empty editable row at the bottom of the task table. The row has: text input for title (auto-focused), priority dropdown (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW, default MEDIUM), status dropdown (NOT_STARTED/IN_PROGRESS/DONE, default NOT_STARTED), date picker for due_date. On pressing Enter in the title field or on blur (if title is not empty), call supabase.from('tasks').insert({ user_id: uid, title, priority, status, due_date }). If title is empty on blur, remove the empty row. Show a spinner on the row during the insert.

todos.title: Delete task with confirmation
todos.description: Each task row shows a trash icon on hover. Clicking it shows a small inline confirmation: 'Delete? [Yes] [No]'. On Yes, call supabase.from('tasks').delete().eq('id', taskId).eq('user_id', uid). Apply optimistic removal from local state immediately, and revert on error. The RLS policy ensures users cannot delete others' tasks even if they bypass the UI.

todos.title: Inline-edit task priority, status, and due date
todos.description: In the My Tasks table, clicking the Priority, Status, or Due Date cell makes it editable (dropdown or date picker inline). On value change, immediately call supabase.from('tasks').update({ [field]: newValue }).eq('id', taskId). Update local state optimistically. Show a subtle pulsing border on the cell during save. This replaces the need for a separate edit modal — all editing happens inline in the table.

todos.title: Search and sort tasks client-side
todos.description: The search input filters the already-fetched task list client-side using task.title.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase()). The Sort By dropdown reorders the array: 'Sort by: Deadline' = order by due_date asc, 'Name' = alphabetical, 'Priority' = HIGH→MEDIUM→LOW, 'Status' = NOT_STARTED→IN_PROGRESS→DONE. These operations are purely in-memory on the tasks array, no new Supabase queries needed.

todos.title: Estimate Deadline AI button
todos.description: The 'Estimate Deadline' button opens a modal. It calls a Supabase Edge Function 'estimate-deadlines' (POST with the list of tasks that have no due_date). The edge function calls OpenAI API and returns suggested dates with reasoning. The modal shows each suggestion with a checkbox. User can accept/reject. On clicking 'Apply Selected', update each accepted task: supabase.from('tasks').update({ due_date: suggestion.date }).eq('id', suggestion.id). Show loading spinner in the modal while the AI call is in progress.

todos.title: Task calendar sidebar — highlight due dates and filter on click
todos.description: The mini calendar in the right column of /tasks should render task due dates as colored dots or short label chips on each date cell. Clicking a date cell sets a dateFilter in state and filters the tasks table to show only tasks due on that date. Clicking the same date again clears the filter. The calendar shows the current month by default with prev/next arrows to change months.

todos.title: Load course list in Academic Load tab
todos.description: Query: supabase.from('courses').select('*').eq('user_id', uid).order('created_at'). Display in numbered table (01, 02...) with: Course Name, Type badge (LECTURE=red, LAB=blue, SEMINAR=pink, ELECTIVE=purple), Credits, Delete icon. Summary cards: Total Credits = sum(credits), Courses Taken = count, Target GPA from profiles.target_gpa. The target GPA card should be clickable to edit the value inline.

todos.title: Add course via '+ Add Course' and '+ Add Another Row'
todos.description: Both buttons append an empty editable row to the course table. Fields: Course Name (text input, auto-focused), Type (dropdown: LECTURE/LAB/SEMINAR/ELECTIVE), Credits (number input 1-6). On pressing Enter or on blur from Name (if not empty), call supabase.from('courses').insert({ user_id: uid, name, type, credits, semester: getCurrentSemester() }). Summary stats (total credits, course count) update immediately after insert. Show spinner on the new row during save.

todos.title: Delete course with cascade handling
todos.description: Each course row has a trash icon. On click, show confirmation modal: 'Deleting this course will also unlink its tasks and schedule slots. Continue?' On confirm, call supabase.from('courses').delete().eq('id', courseId).eq('user_id', uid). Because schedule_slots and tasks have course_id as a nullable FK (SET NULL on delete, not CASCADE), their rows remain but course_id becomes null rather than being deleted. Update summary stats after delete.

todos.title: Load weekly schedule grid in Estimation of Peak Hours
todos.description: Query: supabase.from('schedule_slots').select('*, courses(name, color, type)').eq('user_id', uid). Render a CSS grid with days as columns (Mon–Sun) and hourly rows (08:00–17:00). Each slot block is positioned at its day_of_week column and spans from start_time to end_time rows. Color by course type: LECTURE=yellow, ELECTIVE=blue, LAB=teal, SEMINAR=pink. Show the course name inside each block. Blocks are non-overlapping per column.

todos.title: Add and delete schedule slots in the weekly grid
todos.description: Clicking an empty time cell in the schedule grid opens a small popover form: Course (dropdown from user's courses), Day (pre-filled from clicked column), Start Time (pre-filled from clicked row), End Time (defaults to start+1h), Room (optional text). On submit, call supabase.from('schedule_slots').insert(...). Each existing slot block has an × button that calls supabase.from('schedule_slots').delete().eq('id', slotId) on click. Grid re-renders after changes.

todos.title: Calculate and display burnout summary metrics
todos.description: On Burnout tab load, fetch active and overdue tasks. Calculate client-side: (1) Active Tasks count = tasks where status != 'done'. (2) Deadline urgency: count tasks with due_date within 3 days — HIGH if 3+, MEDIUM if 1-2, LOW if 0. (3) Workload Intensity = min(10, (activeTasks * 0.3) + (overdueTasks * 0.5) + (totalCredits / 30)).toFixed(1). Display in the 3 summary cards with appropriate colors (yellow, black, pink as per design).

todos.title: Burnout probability 7-day trend chart
todos.description: On Burnout tab open: (1) Calculate today's probability = min(100, workloadIntensity * 10 + overdueTasks * 5). (2) Upsert to burnout_snapshots: supabase.from('burnout_snapshots').upsert({ user_id, probability, workload_intensity, active_tasks_count, snapshot_date: today }, { onConflict: 'user_id,snapshot_date' }). (3) Fetch last 7 days: supabase.from('burnout_snapshots').select('probability, snapshot_date').eq('user_id', uid).gte('snapshot_date', today-7).order('snapshot_date'). Render as a red area chart (recharts AreaChart) with X axis Mon–Today and Y axis 0–100%.

todos.title: Detailed per-task workload analysis table
todos.description: Fetch active tasks ordered by workload_impact DESC. For tasks with no workload_impact, calculate it on the fly: HIGH priority = 80, MEDIUM = 50, LOW = 25, then +5 per day overdue. Display each task with: name, a colored progress bar (width = workload_impact%, red if >=70, orange if 40-69, green if <40), risk level badge (CRITICAL >=70, MODERATE 40-69, LOW <40). Update tasks.workload_impact in the DB for any recalculated values.

todos.title: Generate Report button — AI-powered burnout analysis
todos.description: The 'Generate Report' button shows a loading state then calls a Supabase Edge Function 'burnout-report' (POST with userId). The edge function fetches the user's complete task list, 7-day burnout trend, and course load, then calls OpenAI API with a structured prompt to generate a report. Returns { summary, riskLevel, recommendations[] }. Display the report in a modal with a 'Download as PDF' button (triggers window.print() with a print-specific CSS class that hides the rest of the page).

todos.title: Load accepted friends list with presence status
todos.description: Query friendships where (requester_id = uid OR addressee_id = uid) AND status = 'accepted'. For each, compute friend_id = the ID that is not uid. Then join with profiles (full_name, avatar_url, university) and user_presence (status, current_activity, last_seen). Display in the friend cards grid. Status dot: green=ONLINE, yellow=IN_SESSION, gray=OFFLINE. Show 'X Total' badge in the header. Message button is disabled (grayed) when friend is OFFLINE.

todos.title: Real-time friend presence updates
todos.description: On app mount (inside AuthContext or a custom usePresence hook): (1) Update current user's presence to online: supabase.from('user_presence').upsert({ user_id: uid, status: 'online', updated_at: now() }). (2) Subscribe to real-time changes on user_presence for friends: supabase.channel('presence').on('postgres_changes', { event: 'UPDATE', table: 'user_presence' }, handler). On change, update that friend's card in the friends list state. (3) On window beforeunload, set status to 'offline'. Handle tab visibility changes with document.visibilityState.

todos.title: Start Study Session from friends page
todos.description: In the 'Start a Study Session' card, typing searches friends client-side. Clicking a friend adds a chip tag. Clicking an already-added chip removes them. The 'START SESSION WITH X FRIENDS' button: (1) Inserts into study_sessions: { host_id: uid, status: 'active', started_at: now() }. (2) Inserts into study_session_participants for host + each selected friend. (3) Creates a notification for each invited friend: { type: 'session_invite', title: '{name} started a session', body: 'You were invited to study together' }. (4) Updates user_presence: { status: 'in_session' } for host. Then navigate to /session/:sessionId.

todos.title: Direct message chat with a friend
todos.description: Clicking 'Message' on a friend card opens a slide-over panel. Fetch messages: supabase.from('messages').select('*').or(`sender_id.eq.${uid},receiver_id.eq.${uid}`).or(`sender_id.eq.${friendId},receiver_id.eq.${friendId}`).order('created_at'). Display as chat bubbles (user=right/yellow, friend=left/white). Text input + Send button at bottom calls supabase.from('messages').insert({ sender_id: uid, receiver_id: friendId, content }). Subscribe to real-time inserts on the messages channel. On panel open, mark all received messages is_read=true.

todos.title: NEW PAGE: /friends/add — Search and send friend requests
todos.description: Create /src/pages/Friends/AddFriend.jsx. This page is reached by clicking 'ADD NEW FRIEND' card on /friends. Layout: (1) Search section — text input that debounces 400ms and queries supabase.from('profiles').select('id, full_name, email, university, major, avatar_url').ilike('full_name', `%${query}%`).neq('id', uid).limit(10). Show result cards with name, university, and an 'Add Friend' button. On click: insert { requester_id: uid, addressee_id: targetId, status: 'pending' } into friendships if not already friends. Create a notification for the target. Button changes to 'Request Sent ✓' with disabled state. (2) Pending Requests sent section — shows outgoing pending requests. (3) Incoming Requests section — shows pending where addressee_id = uid, with Accept/Reject buttons that update friendship.status.

todos.title: Accept and reject friend requests
todos.description: In /friends/add or via a notification panel, show incoming friend requests: query friendships WHERE addressee_id = uid AND status = 'pending', join profiles on requester_id. Each request shows the requester's name, university, and two buttons: Accept (→ update status = 'accepted', create notification for requester: 'Your friend request was accepted by {name}') and Reject (→ update status = 'rejected'). After accepting, the new friend appears on the /friends page. Pending request badge count shows on the 'Add New Friend' card.

todos.title: NEW PAGE: /friends/:friendId/profile — Public friend profile view
todos.description: Create /src/pages/Friends/FriendProfile.jsx. Route /friends/:friendId/profile, reached by clicking 'View Profile' on a friend card. Verify the viewer is actually friends with this user (check friendships table) — if not, redirect to /friends. Then fetch: (1) profiles: full_name, bio, university, major, avatar_url. (2) user_presence: status, current_activity, last_seen. (3) streaks: current_streak, longest_streak. (4) study_logs count for total sessions. Layout: profile header card (avatar, name, status badge, university, bio), stats row (streak, total sessions), and action buttons: 'Message' (opens chat panel) and 'Remove Friend' (opens confirm modal then deletes friendship row).

todos.title: Load notes list in sidebar and display in two tabs
todos.description: Query: supabase.from('notes').select('id, title, slug, tags, folder, updated_at').eq('user_id', uid).order('updated_at', { ascending: false }). The right sidebar has two tabs: 'Evergreen Notes' (filter notes where tags array contains 'evergreen') and 'Note Taking' (all notes). Each note card shows title and a truncated preview from its first note_section.content. Clicking navigates to /notes/:folder/:slug. The 'New note title...' input creates a new note on Enter key: insert { user_id: uid, title, slug: slugify(title), folder: 'study-space', tags: [] }, then navigate to the new note.

todos.title: Load and display a note in view mode
todos.description: On /notes/:folder/:slug, query: supabase.from('notes').select('*, note_sections(*), note_collaborators(*, profiles(full_name, avatar_url))').eq('slug', slug).eq('user_id', uid).single(). Sort note_sections by order_index. Render note in read-only mode: title as h1, tags as colored pills (evergreen=purple, draft=yellow, idea=green, reference=orange), source as a styled badge, each section rendered by type (heading=h2, paragraph=p, quote=styled blockquote, code=pre/code). Show collaborators' avatar circles in the top-right action bar. Breadcrumb from note.folder.

todos.title: Edit note — title, source, tags, and sections
todos.description: EDIT button switches to edit mode. Title becomes an h1 input. Tags become toggle pill buttons (active = colored). Source becomes a text input. Each note_section becomes editable (contenteditable div or textarea). ADD SECTION buttons (+ heading, + paragraph, + quote, + code, + table, + graph) call supabase.from('note_sections').insert({ note_id, type, content: {text:''}, order_index: maxIndex+1 }). SAVE button: (1) supabase.from('notes').update({ title, slug: slugify(title), source, tags }).eq('id'). (2) For each section: upsert with { id, note_id, type, content, order_index }. CANCEL reverts to last saved state. Navigate to new slug if title changed.

todos.title: Delete note with cascade
todos.description: The DELETE button in the note header opens a confirmation dialog: 'Delete this note? This action cannot be undone.' On confirm: supabase.from('notes').delete().eq('id', noteId).eq('user_id', uid). Because note_sections and note_collaborators have ON DELETE CASCADE on their note_id FK (set in migration), they are auto-deleted. After delete, navigate to /notes and remove the note from the sidebar list state.

todos.title: Share note — public link and collaborator invite
todos.description: SHARE button opens a modal with two options: (1) Copy Public Link: sets notes.is_shared = true, generates URL /notes/shared/:noteId. Create an unauthenticated route that queries if note.is_shared = true (use anon key + RLS policy: SELECT allowed if is_shared = true). Copy URL to clipboard. Toggle to revoke. (2) Invite by name/email: search profiles by name/email, select a person, choose permission (View/Edit), insert to note_collaborators, send a notification to that user. Show current collaborators in the modal with a Remove button.

todos.title: Navigate between notes with prev/next arrows
todos.description: The ← → arrow buttons at the top-left of the note viewer navigate to the previous and next note in the current notes list (sorted by updated_at desc). Using the notes array already in state from the sidebar, find the index of the current note by slug. Navigate to notes[index-1] (prev) and notes[index+1] (next). Disable the button if index is at the boundary. Use React Router's useNavigate() to change routes.

todos.title: Load notifications and show unread badge on bell icon
todos.description: On app load (inside AuthContext or a useNotifications hook): (1) Fetch unread count: supabase.from('notifications').select('id', { count: 'exact' }).eq('user_id', uid).eq('is_read', false). (2) Subscribe to real-time INSERTs on notifications for the current user. When a new notification arrives, increment the badge count and show a brief toast preview. Store the count in a global notifications context so the topbar bell badge always reflects the latest state.

todos.title: Notification dropdown panel on bell click
todos.description: Clicking the bell icon toggles a dropdown panel (fixed position below the bell, z-index above other content). Fetch: supabase.from('notifications').select('*').eq('user_id', uid).order('created_at', { ascending: false }).limit(20). Display each notification with: icon (based on type), title, body (truncated to 80 chars), relative time (2 hours ago). Unread notifications have a yellow-tinted background. Clicking a notification: (1) updates is_read=true, (2) navigates to relevant page based on reference_type (task → /tasks, friendship → /friends/add, message → /friends, session → /session/:id). 'Mark all read' button at top updates all is_read=true.

todos.title: Global search bar with multi-table results
todos.description: The search input in the topbar is visible on all protected pages. On input change, debounce 400ms then run parallel queries if query.length >= 2: (1) tasks: .ilike('title', `%q%`).eq('user_id', uid).limit(5). (2) notes: .ilike('title', `%q%`).eq('user_id', uid).limit(5). (3) courses: .ilike('name', `%q%`).eq('user_id', uid).limit(5). (4) friends via profiles join: .ilike('full_name', `%q%`).limit(5). Show results in a dropdown grouped by type with icons. Clicking a result navigates to that item's page. Press Escape to close. Empty query closes the dropdown.

todos.title: Auto-update streak counter via DB trigger on study_logs insert
todos.description: Create PostgreSQL function handle_study_log_streak(). Logic: (1) Get the user's streak row. (2) If last_study_date = CURRENT_DATE - 1, set current_streak = current_streak + 1. (3) If last_study_date = CURRENT_DATE, do nothing (already logged today). (4) If last_study_date < CURRENT_DATE - 1 (missed a day), reset current_streak = 1. (5) If current_streak > longest_streak, update longest_streak. (6) Set last_study_date = CURRENT_DATE. Create trigger: AFTER INSERT ON study_logs FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION handle_study_log_streak().

todos.title: Manual study time log button on dashboard
todos.description: Add a '+' icon button to the Study Hours stat card on /dashboard. Clicking opens a small modal: Course (dropdown from user's courses, or 'No course'), Duration (hours + minutes pickers), Date (defaults to today, can backfill). On submit, call supabase.from('study_logs').insert({ user_id: uid, course_id, duration_minutes, logged_date }). The streak trigger fires automatically. Re-fetch study hours stat and streak after insert. Show success toast.

todos.title: Active study session page /session/:sessionId
todos.description: Create /src/pages/Session.jsx. Protected route. On mount: fetch study_sessions and study_session_participants joined with profiles and user_presence. Show: (1) Elapsed time counter (now - started_at, updates every second with setInterval). (2) Participant cards with online status. (3) Subject input for host (updates study_sessions.title and user_presence.current_activity in real-time). (4) 'End Session' button visible only if host_id = uid: updates study_sessions { status: 'ended', ended_at: now() }, then calculates and inserts study_logs for all participants, then updates host's user_presence to 'online'. Subscribe to real-time participant changes.

todos.title: Add calendar event by clicking a date cell
todos.description: Clicking an empty date cell in the /dashboard calendar opens a popover form positioned near the clicked cell. Form fields: Title (required), Time (time input, optional), Location (text input, optional), Type (dropdown: exam/homework/lab/seminar/other), Course (dropdown from user's courses, optional). On submit, call supabase.from('calendar_events').insert({ user_id: uid, title, event_date: clickedDate, event_time, location, type, course_id }). The new event chip appears on the calendar cell immediately via optimistic update.

todos.title: Delete calendar event on chip click
todos.description: Clicking an existing event chip on the calendar opens a small popover showing: event title, time, location, and a Delete button. On delete click, show inline confirmation. On confirm, call supabase.from('calendar_events').delete().eq('id', eventId).eq('user_id', uid). Remove the chip from the calendar cell via optimistic state update.

todos.title: Supabase Edge Function: burnout-report
todos.description: Create /supabase/functions/burnout-report/index.ts using Deno. It receives POST { userId } with a Bearer token (JWT). Verify the JWT. Then use the service_role key to fetch: tasks (active), burnout_snapshots (last 7 days), courses, and profiles.daily_study_goal_hours. Build a structured prompt and call the openAI API. System prompt instructs OpenAI to return ONLY JSON. Parse response into { summary: string, riskLevel: 'LOW'|'MODERATE'|'HIGH'|'CRITICAL', recommendations: string[] }. Return this JSON. Store ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in Supabase Vault. Deploy with: supabase functions deploy burnout-report.

todos.title: Supabase Edge Function: estimate-deadlines
todos.description: Create /supabase/functions/estimate-deadlines/index.ts. Receives POST { tasks: [{id, title, priority, status}], today: string }. Calls OpenAI API with the task list in the prompt, asking for realistic due date suggestions for tasks without due dates. System prompt instructs JSON-only response: { estimates: [{ id, suggested_date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', reasoning: string }] }. Frontend displays each suggestion with checkbox in a review modal. User accepts/rejects. Deploy alongside burnout-report.
